Read a questionnaire

Source: R/fct_questionnaire.R
read_questionnaire.Rd

Reads a questionnaire from a csv file, one row per item, for any of the six IRT models of irt_models: the items, their answer options and the coefficients of the item response model fitted with mirt, in mirt's own column names (see questionnaire_from_mirt, which writes such a table from a fitted model). The coefficients are converted to the parameters of the engine of the model. It stops with a message naming the row and the problem, so that a test does not start on a broken file.

Usage

read_questionnaire(file)

Arguments

file

Path to the csv file, saved as UTF-8; or a data frame with the same columns.

Value

The item bank: a data frame with one row per item and the columns scale, item, question, stem, model, n_cat, n_options, options (a list), key, reverse, public, prior_mean, prior_sd and par1, par2, ... (the engine parameters). It can be given to cat_start.

Details

The columns are scale, question and itemtype (required); item and stem (optional); option1, option2, ... (the answer options in scoring order, numbered when absent); key (the correct option of a dichotomous item given as several options); reverse (ordered polytomous items scored in reverse); public (FALSE when the text of the item is not public and only a placeholder is shown, so that the CAT tab highlights the correct option); the coefficients (a1, b1..., c, d, d0..., ak0..., g, u, as mirt names them); and prior_mean and prior_sd, the mean and standard deviation of the latent trait of each scale (0 and 1 when absent).

See also

Other questionnaire: example_questionnaires(), irt_models(), questionnaire_from_mirt(), validate_questionnaire_against_mirt(), write_questionnaire()

Examples

q <- read_questionnaire(example_questionnaires()[5]) # SAT12, 3PL
table(q$scale, q$model)
#>                  
#>                   dichotomous
#>   Science (SAT12)          32
q$options[[1]]
#> [1] "Option A" "Option B" "Option C" "Option D" "Option E"
